Combining

We’ll be using data from the coronavirus package for today’s assignment. The coronavirus dataset has the following columns:

  • date = The date of the summary
  • province = The province or state, when applicable
  • country = The country or region name
  • lat = Latitude point
  • long = Longitude point
  • type = the type of case (i.e., confirmed, death)
  • cases = the number of daily cases (corresponding to the case type)

You need to install and load a package to get the data, so make sure you pay attention to the set up steps and run every chunk.

Set Up

Install the package with the data

# install.packages("coronavirus")

Load the library. Libraries are collections of functions (and sometimes data like here) that are add ons to base R.

library(coronavirus)

We’ll be using data from the coronavirus package for today’s assignment. The coronavirus dataset has the following columns:

  • date = The date of the summary
  • province = The province or state, when applicable
  • country = The country or region name
  • lat = Latitude point
  • long = Longitude point
  • type = the type of case (i.e., confirmed, death)
  • cases = the number of daily cases (corresponding to the case type)

You need to install and load a package to get the data, so make sure you pay attention to the set up steps and run every chunk.

Load the data. The data() loads data from packages into R.

# use the data() function to load the data in the package
data("coronavirus")

Look at the data. Run the chunk and it will give you a nicely formatted preview of the data.

coronavirus %>% head()

Combining dplyr Functions

In this second section, the questions get a little harder. You’ll need to give more than one argument to the dplyr functions and chain multiple functions together. Again, use the code chunk below each question to give your answer.

  1. Find the country with the greatest number of cases so far
coronavirus %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarize(total_cases = sum(cases)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(total_cases))

  1. How many countries do we have data for in the northern (lat > 0) and southern (lat < 0) hemispheres?
coronavirus %>%
  mutate(hemisphere = ifelse(lat > 0, 'north', 'south')) %>%
  select(country, hemisphere) %>% 
  distinct(country, hemisphere) %>%
  count(hemisphere)
  hemisphere   n

Graphics

  1. Make scatter plot
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Color, y = Hue)) +
  geom_point()
  1. add some other parameter in color and shape make scatter plot
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Color, y=Hue, color=Alcohol, shape = Type)) +
  geom_point()
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Color, y=Hue, color= Type)) +
  geom_point()
  1. add fit line and change theme
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Color, y=Hue, color = Type)) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw()
`geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'
  1. make fit line linear
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Color, y=Hue, color = Type)) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm',se = FALSE) +
  theme_bw()
`geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
  1. make boxplot of color split and color by “Type”
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Type, y=Color, fill = Type)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  #geom_jitter(width = 0.25) +
  theme_classic()
  1. make density plot of Alcohol content and split by “Type” to make it more informative make fill transparent with smaller alpha
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Alcohol, color=Type)) +
  geom_density(size=3)
Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead.
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Alcohol, fill = Type)) +
  geom_density(alpha=0.2) +
  theme_classic()
  1. another option to make density plot more readeble is to facet plot by Type, so wi add facet
 wine_data %>% 
  mutate(Alcohol_high_low = if_else(Alcohol > 12.5, "high","low")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Alcohol, fill = Type, color=Type)) +
  geom_density(alpha=0.2) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Type) +
  theme_classic()

Statistics

T-test

  1. to test difference in means we use t test, since with t.test we can only test two groups we will silter one group out in wine example set H0: In stat test we always assume there is no difference
wine_data %>% 
  filter(Type != "Barolo") %>% 
  t.test(Alcohol ~ Type, data = .) %>% 
  tidy()
# A tibble: 1 × 10
  estimate estimate1 estimate2 statistic  p.value parameter conf.low conf.high
     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1    0.875      13.2      12.3      8.78 4.05e-14      102.    0.677      1.07
# ℹ 2 more variables: method <chr>, alternative <chr>
# conclusion there is statistical sig. difference in alcohol content of two winw types
  1. to test more parameter we will use ANOVA
wine_data %>% 
  aov(Alcohol ~ as.factor(Type), data = .) %>% tidy()
# A tibble: 2 × 6
  term               df sumsq meansq statistic   p.value
  <chr>           <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
1 as.factor(Type)     2  70.8 35.4        135.  3.32e-36
2 Residuals         175  45.9  0.262       NA  NA       
# conclusion at least one group is different
  1. to figure out which group is diffenerent we us post hoc test TukeyHSD()
wine_data %>% 
  aov(Alcohol ~ as.factor(Type), data = .) %>% TukeyHSD() %>% tidy()
# A tibble: 3 × 7
  term            contrast    null.value estimate conf.low conf.high adj.p.value
  <chr>           <chr>            <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>       <dbl>
1 as.factor(Type) Barolo-Bar…          0    0.591    0.356     0.826    4.51e- 8
2 as.factor(Type) Grignolino…          0   -0.875   -1.10     -0.649    5.97e-14
3 as.factor(Type) Grignolino…          0   -1.47    -1.68     -1.25     3.10e-14
# conclusion Barolo-Barbera and Grignolino-Barbera are significantly different from each other 
# but groups there is no sig. difference beteewn Grignolino-Barolo btw we could have this idea from boxplot of 
# all Type ploted together

Linear Model (LM)

  1. make a linear model of two parameter from wine data set again H0: there is no correlation Alcohol and Color, these two measurement are independent
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(Color, Alcohol)) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
`geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
wine_data %>% 
  lm(Alcohol ~ Color, data = .) %>% 
  summary() %>% 
  tidy()
# A tibble: 2 × 5
  term        estimate std.error statistic   p.value
  <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
1 (Intercept)   12.0      0.123      97.9  2.18e-155
2 Color          0.191    0.0221      8.65 3.06e- 15
## conclusion there is statistically significant correlation between Alcohol and Color, this to parameters are not independent
  1. if we add type into calculation
wine_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(Color, Alcohol, color=Type)) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
`geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
wine_data %>% 
  lm(Alcohol ~ Color + Type, data = .) %>% 
  summary() %>% 
  tidy()
# A tibble: 4 × 5
  term           estimate std.error statistic   p.value
  <chr>             <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
1 (Intercept)      12.4      0.193      63.9  8.49e-123
2 Color             0.108    0.0243      4.43 1.65e-  5
3 TypeBarolo        0.792    0.105       7.55 2.33e- 12
4 TypeGrignolino   -0.410    0.139      -2.95 3.56e-  3
## conclusion: this is statistically significant correlation between Alcohol and Color apply across all type

Principal Component Analysis

## manipulate dataset
iris2 <- iris %>% 
  mutate(sampe_id=1:n(),
         sample_name=paste0(sampe_id,"_",Species)) %>% 
  select(sample_name, Species, Sepal.Length:Petal.Width)

iris_matrix <- iris2 %>% 
  select(sample_name, Sepal.Length:Petal.Width) %>% 
  column_to_rownames('sample_name') %>% 
  t()

iris_metadata <- iris2 %>% 
  select(sample_name, Species) %>% 
  column_to_rownames('sample_name')
pca_result <- pca(iris_matrix, metadata = iris_metadata)
screeplot(pca_result)
